newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Santer plays down EMU fears after French election.
newsitem.headline: Santer plays down EMU fears after French election.

text.p: The European Commission played down the threat of any change in French policy towards European integration after France's Socialist-led opposition swept to power in parliamentary elections on Sunday.
Arriving for a late meeting of the European Union's executive, Commission president Jacques Santer insisted that economic and monetary union (EMU) was still on track.

Asked by reporters if the French election result could harm the credibility of the planned single currency and its timetable, Santer replied: "No, the timetable is in the treaty... that's an agreement reached at Maastricht and we have to stick to the commitments of the treaty."
Santer said he was in no way disappointed at the French left's triumph and noted that it was a socialist French government that had negotiated the Maastricht Treaty.
"I know what President (Jacques) Chirac's programme is and he's still in office. I look forward to seeing what the new government's programme will be."
Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert also said he saw no reason to doubt EMU's scheduled January 1999 launch-date.
"It seems to be a large (leftist) majority that will be in favour of the euro. I don't think this is going to change anything as far as the euro is concerned," he said.
"As far as we're concerned, the euro is on target and we start on January 1, 1999," added Irish Commissioner Padraig Flynn, arriving for the meeting.
"I don't think the differences in European policies (between the French parties) are enormous," said Finland's Commissioner Erkki Liikanen.

The French Left has stated its conditional support for EMU, but wants a flexible interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty, early membership for Italy and Spain and a European "economic government" to co-ordinate policies inside the euro zone.
Analysts have predicted that, although the Socialists would want to revive debate about what Europe wants from EMU they are unlikely to do anything which might put the project at risk.
